purpose: Close the bounded-occurrence loophole in v1.2. The earlier common-basis proof used EQ3 and EQ4 together, whereas the Tovey hard core only needs occurrence degree at most three. This note proves that EQ3 and positive OR3 alone already forbid one common invertible 2x2 holographic basis that makes both sides matchgate-parity signatures.

setup.basis: Let S=[[a,c],[b,d]] be invertible. Variables transform by S^(tensor 3); clauses by the dual basis (S^(-T))^(tensor 3).
setup.necessary_matchgate_condition: Every matchgate signature has support entirely on even or entirely on odd Hamming parity. For arity three this necessary condition is sufficient for the present impossibility argument; no stronger matchgate identity is needed.

nonzero_entries: If transformed EQ3 is even, its forbidden odd layers give a^2 b+c^2 d=0 and b^3+d^3=0. Invertibility forces a,b,c,d all nonzero.
If transformed EQ3 is odd, its forbidden even layers give a^3+c^3=0 and a b^2+c d^2=0. Again invertibility forces a,b,c,d all nonzero.
normalization.ratio_form: Nonzero row scalings preserve zero/nonzero parity support on both transformed signatures, so normalize a=b=1 and write r=c/a, s=d/b. Invertibility is r!=s.

eq3_constraints.common_consequence: In either parity case r^6=s^6=1. Thus both ratios are sixth roots of unity.

theorem.name: NO_COMMON_BASIS_FOR_EQ3_AND_OR3_MATCHGATE_PARITY
theorem.statement: Over C (hence characteristic zero), there is no invertible 2x2 matrix S for which S^3 EQ3 and (S^(-T))^3 OR3 both satisfy matchgate parity.
proof: If transformed OR3 had even parity, its weight-3 amplitude would vanish, so 3r^2-3r+1=0.
If transformed OR3 had odd parity, its weight-0 amplitude would vanish, so 3s^2-3s+1=0.
The polynomials x^6-1 and 3x^2-3x+1 are coprime over Q. Equivalently, every root of x^6-1 has complex modulus 1, while both roots of 3x^2-3x+1 have modulus 1/sqrt(3).
Therefore neither clause parity is compatible with the sixth-root constraint. Contradiction.
